name: ArtifactsBench
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation. It comprises 1,825 diverse executable queries across nine domains (Game Development, SVG Generation, Web Applications, Simulations, Data Science, Management Systems, Multimedia Editing, Quick Tools, and Others), stratified into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers. The framework renders each artifact and captures its dynamic behavior via temporal (three-step) screenshots, assessed by a Multimodal LLM (MLLM)-as-Judge guided by fine-grained, per-task checklists. It evaluates over 30 leading LLMs and achieves 94.4% ranking consistency with WebDev Arena and up to 90.95% pairwise agreement with human experts.
creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team. ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. arXiv:2507.04952v2 [cs.CL], 2025.
rai:dataCollection: Tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness). Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities, LLM-drafted and human-refined.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control: (i) MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce a 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Solvability validation collected candidate solutions from multiple model families and pruned underspecified items. Execution was standardized with headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024x768 resolution with deterministic seeds, capturing three staged screenshots (before/during/after scripted interaction).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities (five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions). Checklists were LLM-drafted (using Hunyuan-Turbos) and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators; the seed was reused as few-shot references. Human validation used a double-blind protocol: 280 queries with outputs from 6 models were independently scored by multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience, with annotators unaware of MLLM scores and samples appearing in randomized order. The final human ground-truth score represents the median of individual annotators' ratings.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between the automated referee and human experts was measured by pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC), counting concordant pairs out of all unique model-response pairs per query. Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 was achieved among annotators for checklist calibration. Ablation studies examined the effect of including images, multiple screenshots, and model answers on Pair ACC. Cross-judge robustness was assessed by comparing rankings induced by Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B, finding highly consistent partial-order constraints with residual differences concentrated among top-tier systems.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results are open-sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. Dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released. Future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ArtifactsBench provides the community with a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models. It addresses the evaluation gap for interactive visual artifacts, which are central to user experience in modern applications, and offers actionable diagnostics to guide progress in LLM-generated visual code.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark currently focuses on evaluating the quality of the final artifact generated in a single turn, which does not assess agentic or iterative development capabilities. The discrete screenshot sampling approach may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions. Minor discrepancies between referee models are observed in fine-grained scoring of certain complex interactive tasks, reflecting potential cognitive biases in how different MLLMs interpret long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback.
rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior by capturing and analyzing a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions (e.g., multi-step user workflows, nuanced physics in a game). The benchmark focuses on single-turn artifact generation and does not assess agentic capabilities such as iterative refinement, self-debugging, or multi-step development. Purely static items are retained only when visual fidelity or structured graphics are the primary goals.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual code generation tasks. Use cases include: Testing and benchmarking LLMs on their ability to transform multimodal instructions into high-quality, executable interactive visual artifacts; fine-grained capability analysis across nine domains and three difficulty tiers; automated, reproducible evaluation with strong human alignment; and diagnostic analysis of model strengths and failure modes across vision-oriented and code-oriented dimensions.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience served as human annotators for the 280-instance validation study.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini-2.5-Pro (proprietary MLLM referee), Qwen2.5-VL-72B (open-source MLLM referee), Hunyuan-Turbos (checklist generation), Gemini-2.5-Pro (query classification), Playwright/headless Chromium (artifact execution and screenshot capture), MinHash (de-duplication), lightweight classifier (sub-category tagging)
